item.content:encoded: I believe that the article really states that SCP-447 has no effect on dead bodies at all, and that the researcher came up with the zombie virus idea as a way to avoid being around dead bodies.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like the idea, but couple problems:
1. SCP-447-2 being a simple zombie virus seems far to expected to be the most common myth. They already have several SCPs that result in zombies or something similar. I strongly doubt SCP-447-2 is a zombie virus for this exact reason: It seems too simple
2. The O5 council definitely wouldn't accept not being aware of anything within foundation authority.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I havent seen it say that 447-02 makes them into zombies, but in my head ive always felt like it was something much bigger than zombies. Like 447-02 contacts a dead body and the lack of immune response allows the victim to be consumed which leads to production of a new 447-01.
This happening in a cemetary or other place where many dead bodies exist could lead to exponential production of 447-01's and then the world is basically drowning in 447-02.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The way I analyse it is that this may be the original reason for the whole no dead bodies thing, but it could still turn out that it really does do something on contact with corpses. And we were being kept safe by a guy's phobia.

Considering the number of times suggestions of SCP destruction are countered by "For all we know, this thing is keeping us alive", I think this would be an interesting little twist on that theme.

My two units of currency.

item.content:encoded: I kind of like the idea that things like this happen in the Foundation. It seems to me that one of the requirements for promotion to a Researcher or Supervisor rank is some form of incessant neurosis.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I actually like this, for one simple reason: in my head-canon, this has gone on more often than people want to admit. Either researchers can't/won't/forget to do certain things, or they feel they need to "spice it up" either for personal glory or to validate some ludicrous thing that would be needed but not SEEM to be needed, or whatever…

That said, the writing itself is okay. The idea's the part I like.
